meta.titre: Corruption and its Prevention: forms, costs and cures in Cameroon
meta.sous_theme: Meaning, forms, effects and ways of fighting corruption

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A driver is stopped at a roadside and told that his papers will 'sort themselves out' if he slips a note to the officer. A parent hears that a place in a good school may go to the child of someone who pays under the table. Such stories are discussed on radio programmes, in newspapers and in classrooms across the country, because corruption affects roads, hospitals, schools and trust between citizens and the State. The GCE asks you to define it, recognise its forms, explain its effects and propose ways of preventing it, always in a calm, factual tone.

items: Public money comes from taxes and other revenue and must be used for the good of all citizens.
A public servant is a person who works for the State and serves the public.
Honesty means telling the truth and not taking what belongs to others.

sections.titre: Corruption: meaning, forms, effects and prevention
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Meaning
Corruption is the dishonest or illegal use of a position, power or money to obtain a personal advantage, usually at the expense of the public or of other people.

### Forms of corruption
| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Bribery | Giving or receiving money or a gift to obtain a favour or to speed up a service one is not entitled to |
| Embezzlement | Stealing or misusing public funds that one has been trusted to manage |
| Favouritism and nepotism | Giving jobs, contracts or promotions to friends and relatives rather than to the best candidates |
| Extortion | Forcing a person to pay money by threat or abuse of authority |
| Over-invoicing and fake contracts | Charging more than the true cost of a job, or being paid for work never done |
| Examination malpractice | Buying or selling marks, questions or answers |

In Cameroon, bribery is the form most often named: payment to speed up a document, avoid a fine, obtain a job or receive care. Embezzlement, favouritism in recruitment and examination malpractice are other well-known forms.

### Effects
- Public money meant for roads, schools and hospitals is lost, so projects are abandoned or badly built.
- Poor people suffer most, because they cannot pay and therefore receive worse services.
- Justice is weakened when the rich can buy decisions.
- Investors lose confidence, so fewer businesses and jobs are created.
- Citizens lose trust in the State and in one another.
- Unqualified people hold posts, so the quality of public service falls.

### Prevention
- Laws punish corruption, and bodies such as the National Anti-Corruption Commission (CONAC), the Supreme State Audit and the Special Criminal Court work against it.
- Public contracts are published and awarded openly.
- The Constitution provides that certain senior officials declare their assets.
- Fair recruitment by competition, and decent salaries, reduce temptation.
- Citizens refuse to give bribes and report corrupt acts through the proper channels.
- Schools, families, churches, mosques and the media teach integrity from childhood.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how or in what way corruption shows itself
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the form and give a short Cameroonian example without accusing any named person or group. For a 'major way' question choose the form most commonly observed, bribery, and explain it in two or three sentences.

Group effects as economic (lost funds, poor projects), social (inequality, loss of trust) and political (weak institutions). Explain the link: 'Embezzlement of school funds means that classrooms are not built, so pupils learn under poor conditions.'

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how to fight, stop or reduce corruption
variantes.contenu_markdown: Say who acts: the State (laws, audits, courts), institutions and employers (fair recruitment, open tenders), and citizens (refusing to pay bribes, reporting cases). Add one reason why each measure works.

sections.enonce_markdown: Write the model answer to this question: Explain three effects of corruption on the development of a country, and suggest two ways of reducing it. [10 marks]

etapes.justification: 'Explain' needs developed points, and the question has two parts: three effects (6 marks) and two solutions (4 marks).
A definition opens the answer and shows that you know the key term.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Corruption is the dishonest use of position or money for personal gain.

etapes.action: Select three effects from different fields.
etapes.justification: Different fields (economic, social, political) show breadth.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Loss of public funds; injustice and inequality; loss of trust and of investors.

etapes.action: Select two solutions from different actors.
etapes.justification: A good answer shows that both the State and citizens have a role.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Strict enforcement of the law and open public contracts; citizens refusing bribes and teaching integrity.

etapes.action: Develop every point with a reason and conclude.
etapes.justification: Marks go to the point and to the explanation.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Corruption is the dishonest use of a position or of money for personal gain. First, it causes the loss of public funds: money meant for roads, schools and hospitals is embezzled, so projects are abandoned or badly built and development slows down. Second, it creates injustice and inequality, because those who can pay receive better services or avoid punishment while the poor are left behind. Third, it destroys trust and discourages investors, who fear that contracts are decided by bribes, and this reduces jobs. To reduce corruption, the State should enforce the law strictly and award public contracts openly, with audits that check how money is spent. Citizens should also refuse to give bribes and report corrupt acts, and schools and families should teach honesty from childhood. In all, development needs honest management of public resources.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Corruption is when someone steals from a shop.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Ordinary theft is a crime but is not corruption. Corruption involves the abuse of a position of trust or power for gain.
items.correction_markdown: Corruption is the dishonest or illegal use of a position or power for personal advantage.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes that a gift to thank a friend freely is always bribery.
items.pourquoi_faux: A bribe is given to obtain an unfair favour or to influence a duty. A genuine gift of thanks without any such aim is not bribery.
items.correction_markdown: A bribe is money or a gift offered or demanded to obtain an unfair advantage.

items.erreur_markdown: A student answers a question on prevention with 'the police should arrest everybody'.
items.pourquoi_faux: This is not a realistic or lawful measure and gives no real solution.
items.correction_markdown: Suggest lawful measures such as audits, courts, open tenders, fair recruitment and civic education.

items.erreur_markdown: A student blames only public servants and writes that ordinary citizens have no part in corruption.
items.pourquoi_faux: Corruption needs two sides: someone who asks or accepts, and someone who offers or accepts to pay. Citizens who pay bribes also feed it.
items.correction_markdown: State that officials and citizens both have a duty to refuse corrupt practices.

items.erreur_markdown: A student lists effects as 'embezzlement, bribery and favouritism'.
items.pourquoi_faux: These are forms of corruption, not its effects.
items.correction_markdown: Effects include lost public funds, injustice, poor services, loss of trust and fewer investors.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Define corruption. (b) Name two forms of corruption and explain one of them briefly.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Corruption is the dishonest or illegal use of a position, power or money to obtain a personal advantage.** (b) Award a mark for each form, for example bribery, embezzlement, favouritism, extortion, examination malpractice. Example explanation: **Embezzlement is the theft or misuse of public funds by a person entrusted with them.**

items.enonce_markdown: A council has 120,000,000 FCFA to build classrooms that cost 20,000,000 FCFA each. (a) How many classrooms could the council build if no money were lost? (b) Suppose that 30,000,000 FCFA are embezzled. How many complete classrooms can now be built, and how much money is left over? (c) Explain one effect of this loss on pupils.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) 120,000,000 / 20,000,000 = **6 classrooms**.

(b) Money left = 120,000,000 - 30,000,000 = 90,000,000 FCFA. 90,000,000 / 20,000,000 = 4.5, so the council can build **4 complete classrooms**, using 4 x 20,000,000 = 80,000,000 FCFA, with **10,000,000 FCFA left over**, which is not enough for a fifth classroom.

(c) Award a mark for an explained effect: with two classrooms fewer, more pupils must share each room or study in poor conditions, so teaching is less effective and some children may drop out.

items.enonce_markdown: In a small town hospital, patients complain that some staff members demand extra money before giving treatment. Suggest three actions that the hospital administration can take and three actions that patients can take to stop this practice.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for each realistic action and its reason, up to six points. Administration: **(1) display official fees clearly so that patients know what to pay; (2) set up a complaint box or office and punish proven offenders according to the law; (3) supervise staff and organise training on professional ethics and integrity.** Patients: **(1) refuse to pay anything that is not an official fee; (2) ask for a receipt for every payment; (3) report the case to the hospital management or to the competent authorities, for example the anti-corruption commission.** Other valid points: rotating staff, checks by inspectors, awareness talks.

items_markdown: Corruption is the dishonest or illegal use of a position, power or money to gain a personal advantage.
Its main forms are bribery, embezzlement, favouritism and nepotism, extortion, over-invoicing and examination malpractice.
Effects include lost public funds, poor services, injustice, loss of trust and fewer investors.
Prevention involves laws and bodies such as CONAC, the Supreme State Audit and the Special Criminal Court, open public contracts, fair recruitment and civic education.
Citizens have a duty to refuse bribes and to report corruption through proper channels.
Do not confuse forms of corruption with its effects.
